event.title: Wells-Barnett publishes Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases
event.description: A compilation of her investigation into lynching, spurned by the lynching of her close friend.

event.title: Wells-Barnett publishes The Red Record
event.description: According to the Library of Congress, this is the first documented statistical report on lynching.

event.title: Wells-Barnett refuses to walk in the back of the Women's Procession March
event.description: Originally, black protestors were asked to march at the back in order to avoid controversy.

event.title: Wells-Barnett passes from kidney disease
event.description: Her legacy took decades to be fully appreciated, as with many women of color. It is so incredibly important to recognize the impact of Ida B. Wells-Barnett and all she did in the pursuit of justice against lynching.
